attempts.hypothesis: With fixed model dimensions and execution branches, instruction count is approximately a constant overhead plus linear hidden and encoder processing and the self-attention and cross-attention interaction costs.

pcvs.name: hidden_elements
pcvs.rationale: Captures tokenwise normalization, modulation, projections, and feed-forward work at fixed model dimensions.

pcvs.name: encoder_elements
pcvs.rationale: Captures cross-attention key/value projections and key normalization.

pcvs.name: self_attention_work
pcvs.rationale: Captures quadratic self-attention score and value aggregation work.

pcvs.name: cross_attention_work
pcvs.rationale: Captures cross-attention work proportional to video tokens times conditioning tokens.

attempts.hypothesis: The higher instruction count at 27 tokens than at 32 suggests CPU kernel alignment costs. Combining attention interactions frees a feature to capture token tile remainders and may reduce the previous 10.61% irregularity.

pcvs.name: token_tile_remainder
pcvs.rationale: Models CPU kernel remainder handling that can make unaligned token counts more expensive than nearby aligned counts.

attempts.hypothesis: The sixteen-token remainder feature reduced irregularity to 10.09%. Testing eight-token granularity may better explain CPU kernel tail costs, particularly the different behavior of 18 and 27 tokens, while retaining the main processing and attention terms.
